Gold price today, Friday, November 6, 2026: Gold hovers above $4,000 ahead of jobs report

Gold December futures opened at $4,098.50 per troy ounce on Friday, November 6, 2026, declining 0.4% from Thursday's close. As of 7:14 a.m. ET, gold was trading at $4,072 per troy ounce.

Performance changes from opening price: One week ago: +1.6%; One month ago: -1.7%; One year ago: +2.7%. The one-year gain for gold reached 95.6% on January 29.

Gold prices opened above $4,000 for the second consecutive day but are losing momentum ahead of the jobs report. Economists expect employment to rebound from September's 29,000 new jobs figure. The CME Group's FedWatch tool predicts a 72.3% chance the Federal Reserve will raise rates next month. "a strong October employment report could give the Fed more confidence to raise rates next month, a headwind for continued gold price growth."

Expert allocation views: Robert R. Johnson (Creighton University): zero allocation, "tradeoff between slightly dampened volatility and the lost long-term return is certainly not a prudent one". Brett Elliott (APMEX): 2% to 5% for income investors; 10% to 15% growth. Blake McLaughlin (Axcap Ventures): 5% to 8%. Thomas Winmill (Midas Funds): 5% to 15%. Vince Stanzione (First Information): 20%, "gold keeps with inflation and gold retains its purchasing power".
